Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Internationalism (see French monotonie), ultimately from Ancient Greek μονοτονία (monotonía).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈmonoˌtoniɑ/, [ˈmo̞no̞ˌt̪o̞niɑ̝]
  • Rhymes: -oniɑ
  • Syllabification(key): mo‧no‧to‧ni‧a
  • Hyphenation(key): mono‧tonia

Noun

[edit]

monotonia

  1. monotony

monotonia (plural monotonias)

  1. monotony

Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Ancient Greek μονοτονία (monotonía).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /mo.no.toˈni.a/
  • Rhymes: -ia
  • Hyphenation: mo‧no‧to‧nì‧a

Noun

[edit]

monotonia f (plural monotonie)

  1. monotony
  2. (by extension) dullness, tediousness

Related terms

[edit]
  • monotonale
  • monotono

Further reading

[edit]
  • monotonia in Treccani.it – Vocabolario Treccani on line, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana

Noun

monotonia f

Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /mo.no.toˈni.ɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /mo.no.toˈni.ɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /mo.no.toˈni.a/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /mu.nu.tuˈni.ɐ/

  • Hyphenation: mo‧no‧to‧ni‧a

Noun

[edit]

monotonia f (plural monotonias)

  1. monotony (tedium)
    Synonym: tédio
  2. (mathematics) monotony (property of mathematical function)
